differences.title: 1. ARCHITECTURE
differences.leftDesc: RxDB is a full-featured NoSQL database built in JavaScript, running directly in the browser or Node.js with IndexedDB, SQLite, or other adapters, offering offline-first capabilities and real-time sync.
differences.rightDesc: WatermelonDB is a reactive SQLite-based ORM for React/React Native, optimizing performance by only loading visible data and using observable queries for automatic UI reactivity.

differences.title: 2. SYNC MECHANISM
differences.leftDesc: RxDB supports declarative sync via plugins like RxDB-P2P or custom adapters, enabling transparent CRDT-based conflict resolution during intermittent connectivity.
differences.rightDesc: WatermelonDB leverages manual sync operations with optimizations like batching and delta queries to minimize payloads, but lacks built-in CRDTs.

differences.title: 3. PERFORMANCE
differences.leftDesc: Uses RxJS observables for reactive state streaming, ideal for complex multi-source reactivity but may introduce overhead in large datasets due to real-time propagation.
differences.rightDesc: Prefetches and caches only necessary records via observable queries, drastically reducing memory usage and improving performance in large datasets.

differences.title: 4. QUERYING
differences.leftDesc: Queries are schema-agnostic, using JavaScript method chaining for dynamic queries. Schema validation occurs at write time, enabling flexible data structures.
differences.rightDesc: Uses statically typed models with compile-time checks, allowing autocompletion and reducing runtime errors but requiring upfront schema definition.

differences.title: 5. STATE MANAGEMENT
differences.leftDesc: RxDB includes state management via its own observable state trees, enabling seamless integration with UI frameworks without additional libraries.
differences.rightDesc: Relies on external stores like Redux or MobX for global state; WatermelonDB focuses on local state management via observers linked to component lifecycles.

differences.title: 6. OFFLINE CAPABILITIES
differences.leftDesc: Supports full offline operations with conflict-free replicated state transfers (CRDTs) and automatic reconnection handling via sync plugins.
differences.rightDesc: Optimistic UI is achieved via local writes and background sync, but conflicts require manual resolution, relying on app-level logic.

differences.title: 7. DEV EXPERIENCE
differences.leftDesc: Highly configurable with adapters for various storage backends (IndexedDB, SQLite, LokiJS) and sync providers (PouchDB, custom), catering to niche use cases.
differences.rightDesc: Optimized for React and React Native workflows with TypeScript, offering seamless integration into modern frontend tooling but limited to these ecosystems.
